title: Gate or go: an agent on a broken VM, over SSH
part: Part 3 · AI as your co-admin, behind gates
brief: The agent diagnoses three broken VMs through one tool with a read-only allowlist. You are the allowlist; Ansible, run by you, is the only write path.

exercises.prompt: The agent proposes each command below. Allow or refuse? You are graded against the real ALLOW_RE and DENY_RE in agent-over-ssh.sh.
exercises.explain: Read-only diagnostics go through. Anything that mutates, restarts, flushes, changes ownership, downloads, or weakens SELinux is refused and logged, and the agent must propose it as a fix for a human to apply through Ansible.

exercises.prompt: VM 1: metrics-collector crash-loops. The unit says MemoryMax=64M and the process holds 180 MB of buffers. The correct fix is:
options: A drop-in raising MemoryMax and MemoryHigh to a sane ceiling; never edit the vendor unit
exercises.explain: The oracle fix is a drop-in with MemoryMax=512M and MemoryHigh=400M. The test checks that MemoryMax is still set and that the fix lives in a .d/ directory. You wrote it yourself in chapter 4.

exercises.prompt: VM 2: the persisted ruleset has 'tcp dport 2 accept'. The agent proposes `nft flush ruleset` and then re-adding rules. Why does the test fail that approach?
options: The default-drop policy must survive and the persisted file must parse; the fix is edit the file, nft -c -f to validate, then nft -f to apply atomically
exercises.explain: Fix the file first, validate, apply in one transaction, then prove SSH still works from the control host. The lockout this VM is named after happens to people who flush first and think second.

exercises.prompt: VM 3: logrotate silently fails. An agent fixes the `create 0600 root root` line and stops. How many of the planted causes has it found?
options: One of three; the directory ownership and the SELinux context (default_t instead of var_log_t) remain
None; the real cause is disk space
exercises.explain: Three layers, one symptom. This VM tests whether an agent (or you) stops at the first plausible cause. The test checks all three plus no fresh SELinux denials for logrotate.

exercises.prompt: Write the end-of-task report for VM 1 the way the agent has to. All five parts, or the task is not closed.
parts: DONE: what changed, one line per file
VERIFIED: the commands you ran and what they printed
NOT DONE: anything skipped, untested or assumed
ASSISTED-BY: LLM [tool], or 'none' if by hand
exercises.explain: This is the format every agent in your repo must produce. Reviewers read the NOT DONE line first.

exercises.prompt: Run the agent against a broken VM for real. Cleared when the SSH tool's audit log shows at least one command it ran through the gate.
exercises.hint: Boot a VM from one of the cloud-init files first and issue the key with make lab05-key. Then read /tmp/agent-work/ssh-tool.log: every RUN and DENIED line is the agent's real behaviour, whatever its summary says.
